body:
> Please add more features like actionsRef.currrent.reset() to do a full reset of form and field, respectively

Have an issue here tracking this ~ https://github.com/mui/base-ui/issues/1346

> This would make it consistent with the `dirty` and `touched` props which behave in a way that adds/removes attributes

`invalid` is a bit different as it considers the actual validity as well, so when you "reset" to `invalid={undefined}`, it falls back to the internal validity state.

We could possibly accept `null` as a way to reset it, but the current logic works directly with RHF/Tanstack form integrations and it's important to preserve that 🤔 

Are you managing the `invalid` state yourself (e.g. useState) or are you integrating  your field components with other libraries? @DavidCodina

What I'm currently seeing with `Field.Root` is that `invalid={false}` does not set `data-valid` until the `validationMode` has been triggered. Conversely, `invalid={true}` _will_ set `data-invalid` prior to the `validationMode` being triggered.


Similarly, setting `invalid={undefined}` removes `data-invalid`, but if `Field.Root` has `data-valid`, then setting `invalid={undefined}` does _**not**_ remove `data-valid`.

The issue then is that the `invalid` prop exhibits inconsistent behavior. What I expected is that `invalid={undefined}` would result in the omission/removal of `data-valid`/`data-invalid`, regardless of whether or not the `validationMode` has been triggered. 


Initially, I was testing this in conjunction with Tanstack Form, but I also tested `Field` in isolation and got the same result. I haven't tested any other components (e.g., `Select`, etc.), but obviously consistency in behavior is important for all form components.

Maybe, I'm misunderstanding how `Field` was intentionally designed to behave, but it feels off to me. Above you said, that `invalid={undefined}` falls back to the internal validity state. This could be where I'm getting confused. I don't normally interact with constraint validation or ValidityStates.

So... when we "reset" to `invalid={undefined}` the input element still passes native HTML validation and causes `data-valid` to persist because the native ValidityState is valid? If this is the case, then your idea of `invalid={null}` is actually a practical solution. Otherwise, consumers wanting full control over `data-valid`/`data-invalid` through the `invalid` prop may have to resort to hacks like the verbose `useEffect` in the initial code snippet above.

Side note: I also tried to find a way to actually reset the constraint validation to a pre-validation state for a given `<input />`. However, it seems that once constraint validation is evaluated, it can't be reset.

Thanks for your help.
